MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 25, 2020

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Goodell at 5:02 p.m., on February 25, 2020, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 20, 2020, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Kelley
  Mayor Goodell

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Existing Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph 4 of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - Southwest Voter Registration Education Project
  v. The City of Mission Viejo.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Outlined specific dates and actions surrounding the Voters Rights
  Act lawsuit against the City of Mission Viejo and expressed concern that the City is still
  pursuing cumulative voting.

CS2. Conference with Legal Counsel - Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4)
  of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: 1 case

City Council Minutes  1  February 25, 2020
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:07 p.m., Mayor Goodell recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:11 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two matters in Closed Session.
The Council received updates and gave direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Honoring the Late Philip J. Reilly

  Mayor Goodell presented a proclamation to Valley and Sean Reilly.

P2. Transportation Corridor Agency Update

  The Mayor announced that this presentation is postponed until the March 24, 2020, City
  Council Meeting.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Expressed dissatisfaction with the City's handling of the California Voting
Rights Act lawsuit. She voiced concern that the City does not have an election code that lines up
with State law and stated that the voters should determine how to elect their officials.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Raths, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of February 11, 2020, as
  presented.

City Council Minutes  2  February 25, 2020
 2.  Check Register Dated January 31, 2020 in the Amount of $692,768.02

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated February 7, 2020 in the Amount of $803,750.33

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Second Quarter 2019/20

  Received and filed.

5.  Prima Facie Speed Limit on Via Fabricante

  Adopted Ordinance 20-336 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

6.  Civil Engineering Services for Final Design and the Preparation of Working Drawings
  for CIP 20245 (Lower Curtis Park Filtration Basin) and the Overall Lower Curtis Park
  Dirt Receiving Site

  (1) Issued a purchase order to civTEC Civil Engineering in an amount not to exceed
  $65,750.00 for civil engineering design services for the Lower Curtis Park filtration basin
  and the development of the working drawings for the overall Lower Curtis Park fill site
  “Super-Pad", and (2) adopted Resolution 20-05 Amending the Fiscal Year 2019/2020
  Budget for Capital Improvement Program Project 20245 (Lower Curtis Park Filtration Basin)
  and the Overall Lower Curtis Park Dirt Receiving Site to Cover the Cost Of Final Design
  and Engineering for the Stated Project.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Council Member Kelley.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

8.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

City Council Minutes  3  February 25, 2020
 Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum reminded residents the Oso Fit 5K is Saturday, February 29, and
registration begins at 7:30 a.m. She encouraged people to register in advance on-line so they can
choose to donate their registration fee to a good cause by choosing one of many non-profit
organizations. Council Member Bucknum gave kudos to Bob Bunyan who presented a talk on the
history of Mission Viejo this past Sunday. She reminded residents that season openings for Little
League and Softball Leagues are this weekend and she warned drivers to be aware of children in
the parking lots. Council Member Bucknum announced that the Vote Center at City Hall is now
open and she encouraged residents to vote early to avoid crowds.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths thanked Fire and Police Services for all that they do for the community.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs stated that he had no comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley

Mayor Pro Tem Kelley mentioned how many great events happen in Mission Viejo and noted that
she tries to attend as many as she can. On February 18, she, Mayor Goodell and Council Member
Raths attended an event at Saddleback Church for community leaders. Sheriff Barnes was also
there to discuss the many programs Saddleback Church offers for people in the community that
need services. She outlined her attendance at a drug abuse prevention meeting regarding the youth
vaping epidemic and she encouraged parents to get informed. Mayor Pro Tem Kelley discussed
her attendance at additional events including a ribbon cutting ceremony at Fringe Dance Studio,
Mission Viejo Police Services “Securing Our Houses of Worship” program, a tree and shrub
planting event hosted by Oxford Preparatory Academy at Pavion Park, and a Human Trafficking
Presentation. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Kelley reminded residents that the Marine Adoption
Committee has planned a Wine Tasting Event on March 15 from 3:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center. Tickets are $30 and can be purchased at the Community
Center or online at mvcommunityfoundation.org. All proceeds will benefit the City’s Adopted
Marine Battalion.

Mayor Goodell

Mayor Goodell mentioned that the event at Saddleback Church was very enlightening and it was
great to see so many Saddleback Valley cities represented. He announced that he attended the
Olympic Committee Ad Hoc meeting this past week at the Marguerite Aquatics Center and during
that meeting, he learned that the Saddleback College Stadium should be opening at the start of
football season this fall. He also announced that the City is working on a sports tourism website to
attract more events to Mission Viejo. Mayor Goodell reminded residents that the Tyr Pro Series
swimming competition will be held April 16 through 18, 2020, at the Aquatics Complex and it
will include many of the Olympic athletes who will be competing in Tokyo this summer. He noted
that he attended the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Regional Housing
Needs Allocation (RHNA) Symposium with Council Member Bucknum and City Manager

City Council Minutes  4  February 25, 2020
 Wilberg. He and Mr. Wilberg also went to The Ranch in the City of Laguna Beach to get ideas for
a Master Plan for the Casta del Sol Golf Course and he stressed that the immediate band-aids are
being handled out of cash flow from the operations of golf course. In other words, cash revenue
coming in is being put back in to the facility.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 6:58 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Goodell adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 10, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 10, 2020

City Council Minutes  5  February 25, 2020
